claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the trip ran 19.2 km against an optimal 15.5 km, i.e. 3.8 km (+24%) more than the shortest most direct route.

One off-route segment is identified: 12:27–12:36, 5.86 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.69 km, adding 3.17 km and straying up to 1174 m from the optimal route — an unexempted detour segment unless an exemption applies.
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (metered total $40.11 with distance $27.13 for 19.2 km, a $1.41/km rate), so detour kilometres feed directly into the fare, unlike a fixed-quote service.

The driver's claimed reason for the reroute (PIE traffic building up) is not supported by any traffic incident near the route — F12 records no incidents during the trip window, and the trip was in fair weather with 0.0 mm rain.

No traffic-band fact covering the substituted optimal route is recorded as band 1 or 2 (the only bands are band 4, 30–39 km/h, on PIE and CTE), and band evidence alone cannot exempt a segment in any event.
The chat does show the driver asking before the turn-off (12:24, 'go round via Sims Avenue?') and the rider replying 'Sure, go ahead.' at 12:24, which precedes the off-route segment start at 12:27.

However, the rider's agreement was limited to going round via Sims Avenue; the segment actually driven (12:27–12:36) added 3.17 km and departed up to 1174 m from the optimal route, so the consent does not cover the whole of the extra distance recorded.

On the segment not covered by the rider's consent, the rider should recover the metered mileage overcharge, computed as the unexempted extra distance × the trip's per-km rate (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $27.13 ÷ 19.2 km = $1.41/km), per RD-2.
The fare record independently quantifies the excess distance billed: $5.31 for 3.8 km at $1.41/km, giving the judge the computable measure of mileage overcharge on this trip.
The waiting charge was $0.00 and there was no surge (1.0×), so no part of the $40.11 total is explained by a passenger-caused stop, wait, or demand multiplier.

The rider has no history of upheld route disputes (1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld route), so the profile facts do not independently establish the detour and are offered only in support of the refund calculation.

weaknesses: C6 works against us: F7/F8 show the driver asked at 12:24 and the rider agreed at 12:24, before the off-route segment began at 12:27 (F3), so RD-5 exempts at least the portion the rider agreed to and the opposing side will argue the whole segment was consented to.

The only traffic facts are band 4 (30–39 km/h, F10/F11), which the driver will use to argue the reroute was reasonable; RD-4(b) still requires an incident/band-1–2 on the substituted optimal route, and F12 confirms no incident, but a lenient reading could reduce the exempt amount.

We cannot pin an exact 'agreed route' distance, so part of the 3.17 km extra (F3) or the 3.8 km total (F1) may be fairly attributed to the consented Sims Avenue routing, which is why we seek partial rather than full refund.

The rider's own low rating (4.46, F14) and the driver's clean record (4.9, 812 trips, 0 upheld disputes, F15) cut against a narrative of patterned driver abuse and preclude any flag_account request on this profile.

One off-route segment is identified: 12:27–12:36, 5.86 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.69 km, adding 3.17 km and straying up to 1174 m from the optimal route — an unexempted detour segment unless an exemption applies.

The chat does show the driver asking before the turn-off (12:24, 'go round via Sims Avenue?') and the rider replying 'Sure, go ahead.' at 12:24, which precedes the off-route segment start at 12:27.

However, the rider's agreement was limited to going round via Sims Avenue; the segment actually driven (12:27–12:36) added 3.17 km and departed up to 1174 m from the optimal route, so the consent does not cover the whole of the extra distance recorded.

On the segment not covered by the rider's consent, the rider should recover the metered mileage overcharge, computed as the unexempted extra distance × the trip's per-km rate (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $27.13 ÷ 19.2 km = $1.41/km), per RD-2.
